text:
Priya Shah: Uploaded sprinter-7b v2 weights to s3://redwood-models/sprinter-7b/v2/weights.tar.gz — checksum validated. Can we run a quick smoke + catalog bench? I did a quick ingest of tokenizer files too.

Sam Ortega: grabbing them now. quick note — tokenizer/vocab.json looks like byte-level variant, not BPE. saw some weird leading SPACE tokens when tokenizing sentences that start with punctuation. Might affect token counts.

Maya Chen: tagging @Sam @Li — if token counts change, cost estimates in the catalog will shift. do we have a tokenizer test vector to validate? :eyes: 

Priya Shah: added small test vectors under /models/sprinter-7b/tests/tokenizer_cases.txt in the repo. includes edge cases: "...hello", "(foo)", "— em dash". Please run.

Sam Ortega: ran local tokenize check:
```
python -m sprinter.tokenize "...hello"
# output tokens: ['▁...', 'hello']
# token_count=2 expected 1
```
Looks like silent prefix tokenization. Might be new tokenizer config param `trim_prefix_space=false` by default here.

Li Wang: that matches a known byte-level tokenizer change in the upstream model. In our serving we usually set `pretokenize: true` and `trim_prefix_space: true` in catalog config. If we keep false, batch size choices + cost per request go up.

Priya Shah: can we validate config? current catalog entry draft:
```
model: sprinter-7b
weights: s3://redwood-models/sprinter-7b/v2/weights.tar.gz
tokenizer: s3://redwood-models/sprinter-7b/v2/tokenizer/
serve_config:
  max_seq_len: 2048
  quant: int8
  pretokenize: true
  trim_prefix_space: ??
```
What should trim_prefix_space be set to?

Maya Chen: set to true for now to keep token counts consistent with existing catalog models. we should add a note to the model card that tokenizer is byte-level and may have subtle tokenization diffs.

Sam Ortega: ran perf bench on a small fleet (4 x A10G) with typical prompt mix. summary:
- batch=1: median latency 28ms, p99 410ms (spike on kv cache misses)
- batch=4: median 46ms, p99 520ms
- batch=8: median 81ms, p99 980ms (queueing visible)
Also saw higher tokenization time when requests include many punctuation-heavy prompts.

Priya Shah: thanks. can you drop the bench command and raw output so infra can replicate?

Sam Ortega: command and trimmed output:
```
./bench_tool --model sprinter-7b --weights s3://... --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --seq 512 --workers 32 --ramp 60
# results csv: median_ms,p99_ms
1,28,410
4,46,520
8,81,980
```

infra-bot: deploy-check: gpu pool available: 6/8 nodes free. current maintenance window 2024-11-07 02:00-04:00 UTC.

Li Wang: follow-ups:
- set trim_prefix_space: true in catalog entry
- add tokenizer test vectors to model card
- run full catalog perf sweep with batch sizes [1,2,4,8] and seq lengths [128,512,1024]
- add a canary route with fallback to sprinter-6b

Priya Shah: created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/412 — includes config, model card notes, and tokenizer tests. PTAL @Maya @Li @Sam

Maya Chen: quick review done, left one comment about quantization tag naming. none blocking.

Sam Ortega: will run the full sweep tonight and upload csvs to s3://redwood-bench/sprinter-7b/v2/

Priya Shah: great — leaving this thread open for results. thanks all :heart:
